patients.summary: Young unemployed former maintenance worker with recurrent moderate depression, insomnia on trazodone and a long pattern of stopping medicines. An ED visit for arterial priapism in 2025 ends trazodone; in 2026 an ED treats a bleeding coagulopathy after he put out rat poison, which the practice learns of from a pharmacy fill and a late record.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer primary care here; his old office is closing its Medicaid panel. 27M. Main issues per him: depression and trouble sleeping, on one med at night. Insurance verified, Medicaid active. New patient appt set for 8/23 at 9:00. Asked him to sign release so we can get records from prior office; form emailed.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27-year-old man transferring care. Main concerns are low mood and poor sleep.

HPI: Describes depression on and off since his early twenties, with at least two prior stretches bad enough that he stopped leaving the apartment much. Current stretch has gone on most of this year: low energy, little interest, sleeps poorly, appetite fine. Has tried antidepressants through his old office but cannot name them; says he never stayed on any for long because he 'didn't see the point.' Prior office notes (faxed 8/19) list depression, insomnia and repeated missed refills. Sleep: trouble falling asleep, trazodone 50 at night helps when he takes it. No SI now or in the past, no plan, no prior attempts. No mania by history.

PMH: depression, recurrent. Insomnia.
PSH: none.
Meds: trazodone 50 mg qhs.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother with depression. Father with high blood pressure. No bleeding problems or sickle cell in the family that he knows of.
Social: out of work; used to do building maintenance. Shares an apartment with a roommate. Never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Well-appearing, flat affect, good eye contact, speech normal rate. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without bruising or rash. Neuro grossly nonfocal.

PHQ-9 15. GAD-7 8.

Assessment/plan:
1. Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate. Talked through options. He is willing to try sertraline 50 mg daily; reviewed that it takes several weeks and early GI upset usually passes. Gave crisis line number. Video check-in in about a month.
2. Insomnia. Continue trazodone 50 mg at bedtime; I'll take over the prescription.
3. History of stopping medicines on his own: named it with him, plain and nonjudgmental. He agrees to message before stopping anything.
4. Baseline labs today: CBC, CMP, TSH, lipids, HIV and hep C screening.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Asher, all of the blood work from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid, and cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to act on. Keep going with the sertraline and we'll talk next month.

medications.reason: patient stopped on his own after about ten days

documents.title: Telehealth Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he is at his apartment, alone in the room.

Stopped the sertraline after roughly ten days. No side effect he can name, just 'felt the same, so why bother.' Did not message first. Mood about the same as last month. Sleep OK on nights he takes trazodone. Denies SI.

PHQ-9 14.

Not willing to restart an antidepressant right now. Open to seeing someone. Placed referral to outpatient psychiatry, which also has a therapy program. Sertraline off the list. Trazodone continues. Revisit in a couple of months.

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. Screening questions negative, afebrile. VIS given. Waited 15 min, no reaction. Reminded him psychiatry intake office should be calling him.

documents.title: Psychiatry Intake Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient behavioral health clinic, adult psychiatry
Date of evaluation: 01/24/2023
Referral from: primary care, for recurrent depression

Mr. Kane is a 27-year-old single man, not working, who lives with a roommate. He reports several episodes of depression since about 2018, the current one present most of the past year, with anhedonia, fatigue, low motivation and initial insomnia. He has tried antidepressants and stopped each within weeks. He denies suicidal ideation, intent or past attempts. No history of mania or psychosis. No substance use. Mother has depression.

Mental status: casually dressed, cooperative, psychomotor normal, mood 'blah', affect constricted, thought process linear, no SI/HI, insight fair.

PHQ-9: 13.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: trazodone 50 mg at bedtime.

Impression: Major depressive disorder, recurrent episode, moderate. Insomnia.

Recommendations:
- Re-trial of an SSRI. Sertraline 50 mg daily is reasonable; we ask that primary care prescribe and follow.
- Individual therapy here, weekly to start; he has been given a therapist assignment.
- Continue trazodone for sleep.

Thank you for the referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Missed November. Here today after his psychiatry intake on 1/24; their letter is in the chart and suggests trying sertraline again with therapy there.

Has had one therapy session so far, plans to keep going. Mood unchanged. Sleep fair with trazodone. No SI.

PHQ-9 13. Vitals fine. Calm, flat, engaged in the conversation.

Plan: restart sertraline 50 mg daily. We agreed on two things this time: give it six weeks before judging, and send a message rather than quitting. Trazodone same. Back in 2 to 3 months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Medication Adherence Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pharmacy adherence line flagged sertraline: filled once in February, never refilled. Called pt. He confirms he quit it about three weeks in, says it made him 'feel flat' and he didn't want to message about it. No SI. Still seeing the therapist, though he has missed a few. Trazodone he is still taking most nights.

Route to PCP. Sertraline marked as stopped per pt. He will keep the June appointment.

documents.title: PCP Addendum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Will discuss alternatives in June; no change today.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, mood and sleep.

Off sertraline since about March. Doesn't want another antidepressant, including a different class; we went over a couple of options and he listened but is clear. Going to therapy roughly every other week, sometimes skips. Mood a bit better with warmer weather. Takes trazodone most nights, sleeps about six hours. No SI.

PHQ-9 12. Exam: alert, mood 'okay', affect brighter than February.

A/P: Recurrent depression, moderate, not on an antidepressant by his choice. Respecting that; door stays open. Keep therapy going. Trazodone 50 qhs refilled for 90 days. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, 28-year-old man.

Interval: no illnesses. Still looking for work, some applications out. Therapy on and off. Sleep acceptable with trazodone. Not on an antidepressant. Denies SI.

Habits: never smoker, no alcohol or drugs. Walks most days. Seatbelt yes. No firearms at home.

Meds: trazodone 50 mg qhs. NKDA.

Exam: BP and weight at baseline. HEENT clear, TMs normal. Neck without nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no masses. Skin normal. Mood mildly low, affect reactive.

PHQ-9 11.

Plan: no labs needed this year, baseline from last summer normal. Flu, updated COVID and Tdap today (no Tdap on record). Continue current plan for mood and sleep. See me in the spring, sooner if mood slides.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request for trazodone 50 mg #90. Last 90-day fill was in June, so about 3 months overdue; pt says he ran out and "just didn't call." Sent to PCP queue.

documents.title: Refill Approved
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Approved x90 with 1 refill.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in for sleep. Lying awake past 2 or 3 am most nights for about two months, even on trazodone; wanted something stronger. Mood lower since winter. Stopped going to therapy around January. Denies SI, intent or plan; no self-harm.

PHQ-9 16, GAD-7 9. Vitals unremarkable. Tired-appearing, linear, no psychomotor change.

A/P:
- Insomnia: not adding a second sedative. Kept trazodone at 50 mg. Went over a fixed wake time, no screens in bed, getting up if awake more than 20 minutes. CBT-I app info given.
- Depression, recurrent, moderate, worse: offered sertraline again or another agent; declines. Encouraged him to call the psychiatry clinic to restart therapy; he has the number. Crisis line reviewed.
- Follow-up in 2 to 3 months.

documents.title: Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. Missed July follow-up.

Says summer was easier. Sleep improved after he started getting up at the same time each day; still uses trazodone, though not every night. No therapy since winter. No SI.

Never smoker, no alcohol. Not working.

Meds: trazodone 50 qhs. NKDA.

Exam: well, mood euthymic-to-low, affect fuller than April. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin clear.

PHQ-9 10.

Plan: CBC and CMP today since none in two years. Flu and COVID vaccines today. Revisit mood in the spring or as needed.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Asher, your blood count and chemistry panel from the physical are both normal. No follow-up needed for these.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting trazodone 50 mg, 90-day supply. Fill history: last picked up in October. Pt reports he takes it on bad nights only. Pended for PCP.

documents.title: Refill Approved

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his bedroom, camera on.

Mood 'up and down.' Spends a lot of time at home. Sleep varies; uses trazodone some nights, skips others, refills late. Not in therapy. Denies SI.

PHQ-9 13.

Recurrent depression, moderate, untreated by choice; insomnia on intermittent trazodone. Raised medication and therapy again; he'd rather leave things as they are for now. No change. Reach out any time; check back in the fall.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED
Visit: 09/02/2025, arrived 06:50

CC: erection, painful, about 6 hours

30-year-old man woke with an erection around 1 am that has not gone down. Painful. No injury to the groin or perineum, no illicit drugs, no erectile medications. History of depression; takes trazodone at night. No known sickle cell disease or blood disorder, none in the family.

PMH: depression, insomnia. PSH: none.
Meds: trazodone 50 mg qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, not employed (former maintenance worker).

Vitals: normal throughout.
GU: penile shaft fully rigid and tender to touch. No bruising, laceration or other sign of injury. Glans and corpus spongiosum soft, not engorged. Testes normal.

Labs: CBC and basic chemistries unremarkable. UA normal.
Corporal aspiration: bright red blood. Corporal gas pH 7.40, pO2 96 mmHg, pCO2 39 mmHg, consistent with arterial (non-ischemic) flow.

Course: ice packs and observation, no intracavernosal medication. Gradual detumescence by about 10:45. Pain resolved.

Dx: non-ischemic (arterial) priapism.

Disposition: home. Stop trazodone until reviewed by your primary care physician. Outpatient urology follow-up. Return at once for an erection lasting more than 4 hours.

documents.title: Patient Call After ED Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was in the ED yesterday morning for a prolonged erection, resolved there with ice and waiting, sent home. Told to stop his trazodone and see urology. Feeling fine now, no recurrence. Instructed: do not take trazodone, return to ED for any erection over 4 hours. Will request the ED record. Visit booked 10/2 with PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED follow-up. ED record from 9/2 reviewed: about 6 hours of painful priapism, aspirate bright red with an arterial-pattern gas, settled with ice and observation. CBC, chemistries and UA were normal there.

Since then: no further episodes. Has not taken trazodone since that night. No groin injury he can recall.

Sleep is worse off trazodone, taking an hour or more to fall asleep. Mood low, not hopeless. No SI.

PHQ-9 14. Vitals normal. Comfortable, flat.

A/P:
1. Arterial priapism, one episode, resolved. Trazodone discontinued and should stay off. Urology referral placed as the ED advised.
2. Insomnia: no new sleep medicine today. Gave CBT-I workbook and app info, consistent wake time, limit naps.
3. Depression, recurrent, moderate: offered an antidepressant again; declines. Psychiatry clinic number given again.
4. Flu shot today.
Follow-up in 6 to 8 weeks.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, with overnight observation
Visit: 05/12/2026 19:25 to 05/13/2026 10:30

CC: bleeding gums, bruises on arms and legs

31-year-old man brought in by his roommate. Gums bleeding on their own for a couple of days and bruises appearing on his arms and legs. Roommate says he has kept to his room more and more the past few weeks and worries he swallowed something. Patient says he is depressed. On further questions, he had been setting out a store-bought rat poison around the apartment several days ago. Denies prescription medicines or supplements now. Seen here last September for priapism.

PMH: depression, recurrent; insomnia; history of not taking medicines as prescribed; priapism 2025.
Home meds (from prior record): trazodone 50 mg qhs. Patient denies taking any.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: no alcohol. Never smoker.
Family: no bleeding disorders or sickle cell disease.

Vitals within normal limits on arrival and through observation.
Exam: multiple ecchymoses over both upper extremities. Slow oozing at the gum line. No petechiae. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen enlargement. Neuro intact.

Labs: platelets 180,000/uL. PT 24 s. PTT 61 s. Bleeding time 5 min. Serum tox screen negative for opioids, benzodiazepines and acetaminophen.

Psychiatry consult (evening of 5/12): depressed mood, cooperative. Denies suicidal intent, thoughts of self-harm, or intentional ingestion; describes the exposure as happening while he was putting out the bait. Not felt to need inpatient care. Advised outpatient behavioral health follow-up; resources given.

Course: vitamin K1 10 mg IV. Observed overnight; gum oozing stopped by morning, no new bruising.

Dx: rotenone poisoning, accidental, with coagulopathy.

Disposition: home with roommate. Vitamin K1 5 mg by mouth daily, prescription sent. INR recheck with primary care in a few days. Remove remaining bait from the apartment. Return for any bleeding.

documents.title: Pharmacy Fill Notice
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fill history update: vitamin K1 (phytonadione) 5 mg tabs filled 5/13/26, prescriber from a regional hospital ED. No ED notification received here. Called pt, no answer, voicemail full. Sent portal message asking him to call. Front desk to request ED records.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to regional hospital HIM for any ED/observation records from May 2026.

documents.title: Patient Returned Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt returned call. Went to the ED earlier this month for bleeding gums and bruises after putting out rat poison at home. Kept overnight, given vitamin K. Says the bleeding has stopped and he's taking the pills. Does not recall being told about a blood test. Advised he needs a visit and an INR check soon. He will call back to schedule once he knows his ride. Asked him to call 911 or go back to the ED for any bleeding.

documents.title: Records Request, Second
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Nothing received from the May request. Re-faxed to the hospital records office and called; they say it is in queue.

documents.title: RE: Need appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Asher, you're booked Tuesday 9/8 at 10:20 with your doctor. If things feel worse before then, call us, and for a crisis call or text 988.
